definition: Determining which enrolled speaker produced an audio segment, using voice embeddings such as x-vectors or d-vectors.
details: Determining which enrolled speaker produced an audio segment, using voice embeddings such as x-vectors or d-vectors. Distinct from diarization, which segments “who spoke when” without identities.

explainer.lead: Speaker identification determines which enrolled speaker produced an audio segment, using voice embeddings such as x-vectors or d-vectors. It matters because it attaches a known identity to speech, which diarization alone does not do.

tiers.eli5: It is like hearing a voice and picking out which of the people you already know it belongs to.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers compare a segment's voice embedding against embeddings of enrolled speakers to find the match. A pitfall is confusing it with diarization, which segments who spoke when without assigning identities.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as determining which enrolled speaker produced an audio segment, using voice embeddings such as x-vectors or d-vectors; distinct from diarization, which segments who spoke when without identities. No formula or stated limits are given.

explainer.example: Given a recording and a set of enrolled voices, the system extracts an x-vector from the segment and returns the enrolled speaker whose voice embedding it best matches.
